scope: projectable HMT gravitational constrained sector only; lambda=1 branch; no DSIR; no matter-interface coefficient selection
scientific_question: Does the vanishing of the flat-linearized second-class kernel at lambda=1 imply a new first-class symmetry, or is it only a linearization/rank degeneracy of the exact source-locked constraint pair?

source_locked_input.reference: J. Kluson et al., U(1) Invariant F(R) Horava-Lifshitz Gravity, arXiv:1012.0473, Sec. 5
source_locked_input.HMT_limit: F'(A)=1 after auxiliary-field reduction, for which the remaining Hamiltonian structure is identified with non-relativistic covariant/projectable HMT Horava-Lifshitz gravity
source_locked_input.Phi1II: (1/kappa^2) sqrt(g) G(R); for the HMT curvature constraint take G'(R) nonzero and flat background obeying G(0)=0
source_locked_input.Phi2II_exact_HMT_limit: -2 R_ij pi^ij + [2 lambda/(D lambda-1)] R pi + [(1-lambda)/(lambda D-1)] nabla^2 pi
source_locked_input.source_constraint_classification: Phi1II and Phi2II are identified as second-class in the full Hamiltonian analysis; preservation fixes multipliers and no additional constraint is generated in the generic full phase-space analysis

frozen_branch.background: flat periodic T^3 with R_ij=0, R=0, pi^ij=0, N=N(t), A=0, nu=0 gauge
frozen_branch.zero_mode_policy: k=0 remains outside local invertibility claims
frozen_branch.perturbation_order_policy: track the first nonvanishing perturbative order of Phi2II and of the bracket; do not infer first-class status from a vanishing linearized bracket alone

frozen_derivation_checks: substitute lambda=1 into the exact HMT-limit Phi2II and verify that the nabla^2 pi term vanishes exactly
derive Phi2II(lambda=1) = -2 R_ij pi^ij + 2/(D-1) R pi
on the frozen flat zero-momentum background classify Phi1II as starting at O(h) and Phi2II(lambda=1) as starting at O(h*pi), hence Phi2II has no nonzero linear perturbation
verify that the previously obtained flat-linearized C12 vanishes for lambda=1 because the only O(pi) term in Phi2II is absent
distinguish linearized rank loss from a proof of first-class closure
use the source-locked full Hamiltonian classification as evidence against promoting the pair to first-class without a dedicated exact lambda=1 closure theorem
classify the flat lambda=1 point as an irregular/linearization-degenerate constrained background if these checks hold

allowed: PASS_SCOPED if lambda=1 removes the linear O(pi) term while the exact constraint retains curvature-times-momentum terms, establishing that flat-linearized rank loss does not by itself prove a new gauge symmetry
report that the exact first nonzero Phi2II contribution is at least quadratic in perturbations around the frozen flat zero-momentum background
report that a nonflat or nonzero-background-momentum expansion is required to recover a nontrivial local bracket at leading order
forbidden: claim a new exact first-class symmetry at lambda=1 without computing exact closure
claim that lambda=1 HMT is inconsistent or ruled out
claim that the full Faddeev-Senjanovic determinant is computed
import ordinary projectable-Horava beta functions into HMT
change any previously frozen RTK threshold
